newEntries: PHB p. 19, Table II: any armor or shield; club, flail, hammer, mace, or staff; oil is allowed. Poison is barred to non-evil clerics; an evil cleric needs referee permission. The starred weapon note includes magical weapons unless the item itself bars the class.
PHB p. 20: cleric spells must be spoken or read aloud, and clerics cannot use edged or pointed weapons.

PHB p. 19, Table II: leather armor, wooden shield; club, dagger, dart, hammer, scimitar, sling, spear, or staff; oil is allowed. The poison ? is referee-dependent. The starred weapon note includes magical weapons unless the item itself bars the class.

PHB p. 21: druids cannot turn or control undead, demons, or devils. At 7th level a druid can change form up to three times per day, once per creature type (reptile, bird, or mammal); the assumed creature retains the druid’s mind. Forms range from a bullfrog, bluejay, or bat to a large snake, eagle, or black bear about twice the druid’s weight. Each change heals 10–60% of damage sustained before changing form.
PHB pp. 21, 34: druids have a separate secret tongue, in addition to the common, alignment, and other languages they know.

PHB p. 19, Table II: any armor, shield, or weapon; oil is allowed and poison is referee-dependent. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).
PHB p. 22: Strength above 15 grants a 10% bonus to experience awarded. The fighter may be of any alignment.

PHB p. 19, Table II: any armor, shield, or weapon; oil is allowed; poison is never allowed. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).

PHB pp. 22, 24: a paladin may retain at most 10 magic items (1 suit of armor, 1 shield, 4 weapons, 4 other items); a magic bow and magic arrows together count as one weapon. The paladin retains only enough wealth for a modest lifestyle, henchmen/servants, and a small castle; gives away excess and tithes 10% of all income to a lawful-good charitable religious institution, and attracts no men-at-arms.

PHB p. 19, Table II: any armor, shield, or weapon; oil is allowed and poison is referee-dependent. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).

PHB p. 24: underground tracking requires observing the creature within 3 turns and starting at the place observed; outdoors the base chance is 90%, modified by party size, elapsed time, and precipitation. Use the separate listed action chances underground.

PHB pp. 24–25: a ranger adds one point of melee damage per experience level against listed giant-class humanoids, surprises opponents 50% of the time, and is surprised 16 2/3% of the time. No more than three rangers may operate together; level-10 followers are 2–24 and cannot be replaced.

PHB p. 19, Table II: no armor or shield; dagger, dart, or staff; oil is allowed and poison is referee-dependent. The starred weapon note includes magical weapons unless the item itself bars the class.

PHB p. 25: a cast spell must be regained by consulting its proper spellbook before it can be cast again; all spells must be spoken or read aloud. Spellbooks must be maintained as new spells become usable.

PHB p. 19, Table II: no armor or shield; dagger, dart, or staff; oil is allowed and poison is referee-dependent. The starred weapon note includes magical weapons unless the item itself bars the class.
PHB p. 26: use the Illusionist-specific magic-item permissions; the listed magic-user scrolls are usable only when they contain spells the Illusionist can use.

PHB p. 19, Table II: leather armor, no shield; club, dagger, dart, sling, and short/broad/long sword (not bastard or two-handed); oil is allowed and poison is referee-dependent. Apply the p. 19 weapon-type note.

PHB p. 28: a percentile result equal to or below the adjusted chance succeeds. Each lock gets one attempt until the thief gains a level; locating and removing a trap are separate rolls with one attempt per thief; listening takes a full minute; a failed language can be retried after gaining a level.
PHB pp. 27, 34: all thieves know Thieves’ Cant in addition to other languages they may learn through race or Intelligence.

PHB p. 19, Table II: leather armor, any shield or weapon; oil and poison are allowed. The any*** row restricts characters under 5 ft. from longbows or weapons over 12 ft., and characters under 100 lb. from heavy crossbows or pole arms over 200 gp weight (including two-handed swords).

PHB p. 29: poison placement and timing must be specified for the referee to adjudicate, and a poisoned weapon may be noticed. The minimum-fee table is keyed by assassin level and victim-level bracket; important, popular, or noble victims may count above actual level. Fees are separate from XP awards.

PHB p. 19, Table II: no armor or shield; bo sticks, club, crossbow, dagger, hand axe, javelin, jo stick, pole arm, spear, or staff; oil is not allowed and poison is referee-dependent. The starred weapon note includes magical weapons unless the item itself bars the class.

PHB p. 30: open-hand attacks can stun or kill. A stun requires a hit roll at least 5 above the minimum required and lasts 1–6 melee rounds. Killing is a separate percentile roll: the monk must first hit and stun, then roll equal to or below the opponent’s AC modified by the monk’s levels above 7; the source notes a negative chance at AC −1.

PHB p. 32: quivering palm is a separate ability, attempted only once per week; the monk must touch the intended victim within 3 melee rounds or the power is drained for one week. It has no effect on undead or creatures hit only by magical weapons; the victim cannot have more hit dice than the monk, and its hit points cannot exceed the monk’s by more than 200%. The death command must come within one day per monk level at use or the vibrations cease harmlessly. The general monk restriction is no Strength bonus to hit probability or damage.
